Unlike other kernel methods like Epanechnikov, Gaussian kernels have infinite support, which requires clipping to maintain efficiency [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that Gaussian kernels have infinite support, which requires clipping to maintain efficiency, and contrasts this with Epanechnikov kernels. Source [S1] explicitly notes in the bullet points that 'Gaussian kernels have infinite support, requiring clipping to avoid evaluating all primitives, which reduces efficiency.' Additionally, the Japanese text under 'Kernel Comparison' states that 'Gaussian kernels have continuous (infinite) support... whereas Epanechnikov kernels have finite support, resulting in more compact primitives and improved acceleration structure efficiency and rendering speed.' Thus, all facts in the claim are present and supported by the evidence.
